newsitem.title: UK: UK clears CE Electric bid for N Electric.
newsitem.headline: UK clears CE Electric bid for N Electric.

text.p: The British government has cleared the 782 million pounds ($1.29 billion) hostile takeover bid from U.S. utility CE Electric for Northern Electric Plc, said Ian Lang, UK Trade and Industry Minister on Friday.

The clearance comes ahead of next Friday's closure of the 650 pence-per-share offer for Northern, which has slammed the offer as too low. Lang said in a statement: "CE Electric has given me assurances to address the regulatory concerns...These include assurances relating to Northern's financial and management resources and to maintaining Northern's financial status."
UK clears CE Electric bid for N Electric

CE Electric welcomed the decision. It said in a statement "The decision for shareholders is now crystal clear. In contrast to Northern Electric's board's suggestion that shareholders should forgo cash for their shares and instead wait to see what an uncertain future holds, CE Electric's final offer...is real and certain today."
The uncertainty over whether the hostile bid would be given the green light has taken the spark out of the British utility's shareprice.
But just after the announcement, Northern Electric's share price leapt 38 1/2 pence to 641 pence.

Lang said that with the assurances received he agreed with the British competition watchdog, the Office of Fair Trading, that there was no need to refer the case to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission for further consideration. CE Electric first launched its bid in October. The offer was raised from 630 pence per share to 650. ($1=.6043 Pound)
